name: MIPLIB 2017 open instance genus-g31-8
description: Find a feasible solution of the MIPLIB 2017 instance genus-g31-8 with as low an objective value as possible (a maximisation model is negated, so that lower is better for every instance). A solution is feasible when every variable bound, every row bound and the integrality of every integer variable hold within an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 on the values as they are returned; integer variables are not rounded first.

sources.locator: A Practical Method for the Minimum Genus of a Graph: Models and Experiments
Gleixner et al. (2021), MIPLIB 2017: data-driven compilation of the 6th mixed-integer programming library (benchmark paper, not evidence).
Instance pages with submitter, group, status and best known objective.

execution.interface: solve(model) -> numpy array of num_cols values, one per column. model has name, mps_path (the uncompressed MPS file), num_cols, num_rows, A (scipy CSR matrix of the rows), col_cost, col_lower, col_upper, row_lower, row_upper, integrality (bool array), offset, maximise and indicators (a list of (row, column, value): such a row has to hold only when that column equals the value; empty for most instances). Score: col_cost @ x + offset in minimisation form (negated when maximise is true), minimized; an infeasible vector is invalid.

limitations: The objective listed on the open-instances page may have been improved since 2026-11-11 (the list did not change between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-11).
Candidates may call HiGHS through highspy; a stronger solver is a method, not a discovery by the workflow.
The record was reproduced by this task's verifier from a published solution (or an optimiser run). See VALIDITY.md.

checks: the published solution, checked by our verifier: feasible within 1e-6, objective -23.0

science_relevance.reason: The cited paper's main objective is computing the minimum genus of a graph with integer programming models, which is the problem the evaluator scores on these instances.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find an embedding of the graph genus-g31-8 (an AT&T/North or Rome graph) on an orientable surface of smallest genus, in the integer programming model of the minimum-genus problem.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Minimum genus is NP-hard and a basic parameter of topological graph theory with no standard practical exact method before ILP models; open instances here mean the optimum is not proven or not found.

papers.title: A Practical Method for the Minimum Genus of a Graph: Models and Experiments
papers.task_relation: The task is one instance of an ILP model of this problem on a graph from the North or Rome collections (the page names these collections; the exact model variant is the submitter's and was not compared line by line with the paper).
papers.primary_goal: Develop and experimentally compare integer programming models and a practical exact method for computing the minimum genus of a graph.
